metaTitle: Krachi Yam Festival at Kete Krachi, Oti Region
metaDescription: The Krachi Yam Festival brings Kete Krachi and its yam-growing neighbours together in September: a week of events, masquerades, open yam pounding and a durbar led by the Krachiwura.
subtitle: Thanks for the yam harvest
answer: The Krachi Yam Festival is held each September at Kete Krachi in the Oti Region to welcome the new yam and give thanks for the harvest. It runs for a week of cultural and social events and ends with a durbar led by the Krachiwura, with masquerades and yam pounded in the open as a sign of a good harvest.

sections.title: What happens
sections.html:
The festival welcomes the new yam with a week of cultural and social events, ending in a durbar of chiefs and people led by the Krachiwura, Nana Mprah Besemuna III.[[1]] At the 2015 durbar there were masquerades and an open pounding of yam as a sign of a bumper harvest.[[2]]

The Krachiwura has said the festival was set up to bring the Krachi and their yam-growing neighbours together to thank God for the harvest, alongside the older Nanaba festival rather than in place of it.[[2]]

sections.title: Good to know if you go
tips: Where: Kete Krachi is the capital of Krachi West. See the Oti page for places nearby.
Check the dates: the traditional council sets them each year. Local radio and the national press carry the announcement.
Respect the rites: some rituals are sacred and not for cameras. Ask before photographing chiefs, priests or anyone taking part, and follow what the ushers ask.
